claims.text: For Pacific islands in 2026, the joint aggregate mean (expected) revenue loss is the signed mean of the simulated distribution, averaging gains and losses across all draws.
For Pacific islands in 2026, the aggregate ES95 is the average loss in the worst tail of the joint aggregate distribution, measured on positive shortfall only.

The two measures differ because the mean is a signed quantity averaged over the entire distribution, including draw outcomes where event revenue exceeds neutral revenue, whereas ES95 conditions on the extreme loss tail of the aggregate positive shortfall. The tail concentrates outcomes where adverse climate dependence and shared-year shocks combine across islands, so the expected shortfall substantially exceeds the signed mean. Aggregate risk uses common simulation draws; country quantiles are never summed.

limitations: Historical input provenance is incomplete; the assessment is for inspection only and is not recomputable.
Estimates are event-conditional, not observed losses or a validated official budget forecast; the fiscal model estimates historical associations and does not identify a causal tax multiplier.
Monetary units are constant 2025 USD, GDP-deflated, at a fixed 2025 exchange rate; price and exchange-rate responses are not modeled.
Aggregate ES95 is computed on the joint aggregate distribution with common simulation draws; it is not the sum of country tail measures.
The signed mean retains gain outcomes, so it is not directly comparable to the positive-part ES95 shortfall.
arguments.title: Pacific islands expected loss versus ES95 in 2026
